page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ce4.xlarge is an x86_64 compute instance belonging to the High Clock Speed family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor operating at 3.2 GHz, configured with 2 physical cores and 4 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading. The virtual machine includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. Hardware acceleration flags include AVX, FMA, BMI2, and AES-NI, but lack AVX-512 and AMX instructions. The instance operates on the KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. It contains no bundled local storage and has no discrete GPUs, requiring external cloud block storage for persistent data.

Benchmark results reflect the older Broadwell architecture of the Xeon E5 v4 family. The instance achieved 1,154 in Geekbench 6 single-core and 2,449 in multi-core testing, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 4,229.29 and stress-ng scores that place it in the lower quartile of modern cloud instances. Memory performance demonstrates uncached sequential read throughput of 22.44 GB/sec and write throughput of 14.99 GB/sec. Despite lower raw multicore compute and memory bandwidth, single-threaded throughput shows stability in legacy tasks, registering 25.96 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 80.49 tokens per second for small-model language generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.ce4.xlarge delivers substantial memory density relative to its vCPU footprint, but its older microarchitecture offers reduced compute throughput per resource compared to newer instance generations. With no bundled local storage and a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps, network and I/O-intensive workloads may encounter bottlenecks. The configuration is primarily aligned with memory-heavy legacy services, low-concurrency backend services, caching tiers, or development environments that require a high RAM-to-CPU ratio without requiring advanced vector instruction support.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ce4.xlarge is a High Clock Speed family virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture. Driven by a dedicated 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor, it provides 2 physical cores, 4 vCPUs, and 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU allocation. The instance features no bundled local storage, requiring network block storage, and operates with a 2 Gbps baseline network throughput without GPU acceleration. Benchmark results show legacy computing metrics, with Geekbench single-core at 1,154 and multi-core at 2,449, alongside lower-quartile uncached memory bandwidth. It maintains acceptable performance in single-threaded operations such as gzip compression at 25.96 GB/sec. Given its high RAM allocation relative to vCPUs, ecs.ce4.xlarge is suited for memory-intensive background workloads, intermediate caching layers, and staging environments that do not demand cutting-edge CPU compute density.
